message.content:
In the repo /opt/nxeon, verify the CURRENT source state of these five claimed "reports success without verifying it" defects. The claims come from a doc that may be stale — READ THE CODE and report exactly what is there now, with exact line numbers and verbatim evidence lines. Do NOT edit anything.

For each item report: (a) is the claim still TRUE in current source? (b) exact line numbers + verbatim evidence line(s), (c) the containing function/export, (d) any verification that already exists which the claim missed.

7. `lib/actions-domains-advanced.ts` lines ~133-152 (`setWhoisPrivacy`) and `app/dashboard/domains/[id]/page.tsx` line ~115 — claim: setWhoisPrivacy writes a local boolean and never contacts the registrar, and the domain checklist renders a green tick "WHOIS privacy on" from the raw DB flag, so it reports a preference as if it were registrar state.

8. `worker/databases.ts` lines ~111-130 (`dbCreate`) — claim: the database is marked ACTIVE on `CREATE` exiting 0 as root, never a login probe with the generated password, and `passwordEnc` is nulled immediately so nobody can re-derive it. ALSO: read `worker/apps.ts` around lines 465-520 (`provisionDb`) which is said to contain "the exact probe this needs" — report its exact code shape and the helper functions it uses (`execInput`, `exec`, `why`, `shellQuote`, `assertIdent`) and where those helpers are defined (which file, exported or not).

9. `lib/actions-email-hosting.ts` line 5 and lines ~463-478 — claim: email-domain ownership verification (the gate that grants mailbox creation) uses the bare top-level `resolveTxt`/`resolveMx` from node:dns, i.e. the system resolver, rather than an authoritative one. ALSO read `lib/mail/deliverability.ts` lines ~1-60 which is said to do it correctly — report the exact exported helper name(s) there that resolve authoritatively and their signatures, so they can be reused.

10. `worker/index.ts` lines ~270-330 (the `provision` handler tail) — claim: the cloud-init snippet write failure is swallowed with `.catch` at ~276-278, and readiness (guest booted / sshd listening) is never probed before writing RUNNING at ~318 and notifying with a copy-pasteable `ssh root@…` at ~323.

11. `worker/index.ts` lines ~105-120 — claim: the Claude Code install is `npm install -g … || true` and nothing records the result, while 7 places in the product assert "Claude Code is pre-installed on every Nxeon server". Report the exact surrounding function and how that generated script is delivered (cloud-init? snippet?), and grep for where the 7 claims live (just list the files/lines).

Return a compact per-item report. Quote only load-bearing lines. Use absolute paths.

content.text:
All five verified against current source. Report below.

---

## 7. WHOIS privacy — **CLAIM TRUE** (both halves)

**(a) TRUE.** `setWhoisPrivacy` contains zero registrar I/O.

**(b) `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-domains-advanced.ts`** — function `export async function setWhoisPrivacy(` at **line 133**, ends line 152. The entire body's only side effect:
```
139:  await db.domain.update({ where: { id: domainId }, data: { whoisPrivacy: enabled } });
```
No `nc(...)` call (the name.com client is defined at lines 14–41 of the same file and is used by the nameserver/transfer paths, e.g. line 104 `Registrar rejected the update:` — so the omission is local to this function, not the file).

**(c)** Containing export: `setWhoisPrivacy` (server action, `"use server"` at line 1). Caller: `WhoisPrivacySection` in `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/DomainAdvanced.tsx:142` (invoked line 161).

Checklist half — **`/opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/domains/[id]/page.tsx:115`**, verbatim:
```
115:    { label: "WHOIS privacy on", done: domain.whoisPrivacy, hint: "Turn on WHOIS privacy under Advanced." },
```
Containing export: `default async function` domain detail page; array `const checklist: ChecklistItem[]` starts line 97. Renderer `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/DomainChecklist.tsx:41` — `{item.done ? "✓" : ""}` with `border-emerald-500/50 bg-emerald-500/15 text-emerald-300` (line 37). Green tick confirmed. Note the DB default is `@default(true)` (`/opt/nxeon/prisma/schema.prisma:217`), so the tick is green on every domain from creation, registrar or not.

**(d) Verification the claim missed:** the action *does* return an honest disclaimer string, and the UI renders it:
```
150:    note: `Preference saved (${enabled ? "on" : "off"}). WHOIS privacy at ${domain.registrar} is provisioned at registration — contact support to change it on a live domain.`,
```
rendered at `DomainAdvanced.tsx:199`. Also the doc comment at lines 128–132 states the persisted-only intent explicitly. So the *Advanced tab* is honest; the **checklist at page.tsx:115 is the sole place that launders the preference into an asserted registrar fact**, and it never sees that note.

---

## 8. `dbCreate` marks ACTIVE without a login probe — **CLAIM TRUE**

**(a) TRUE**, on both counts.

**(b) `/opt/nxeon/worker/databases.ts`**, `export async function dbCreate(job: Job)` at **line 88**. The only success criterion is the CREATE exit code:
```
111:          const r = await execInput(conn, "mysql --protocol=socket -uroot", sql, SETUP_TIMEOUT_MS);
112:          if (r.code !== 0) throw new Error(`MySQL create failed: ...`);
```
(postgres equivalent at 120–121), then unconditionally:
```
126:    await db.vpsDatabase.update({ where: { id: row.id }, data: { status: "ACTIVE", error: null, passwordEnc: null } });
```
`passwordEnc: null` is on the same statement as `status: "ACTIVE"` — and the failure path nulls it too (line 136). Password lifecycle: written once at `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-databases.ts:152` (`passwordEnc: encryptSecret(password)`), decrypted once at `worker/databases.ts:97`. After line 126 it is unrecoverable, so a non-working credential can never be diagnosed or re-tested.

**(c)** Containing export: `dbCreate`, registered as the `DB_CREATE` job handler (per header comment lines 20–33).

**(d) Missed verification:** `dbCreate` is not verification-free everywhere — `ensureMysql`/`ensurePostgres` (lines 68, 77) do check install exit codes, and `assertIdent`/`assert` run at 92–94. The gap is precisely the login probe.

### The probe that already exists — `provisionDb`

**`/opt/nxeon/worker/apps.ts`**, `async function provisionDb(` at **line 471** (module-private, not exported). Its doc comment at 465–470 names the exact defect:
> `then PROVE that credential works by connecting with it. … "the CREATE statement exited 0" is not evidence that it will log in.`

Shape (MySQL branch, lines 490–506): run the CREATE via `execInput`, check `r.code !== 0`, then a second `execInput` that streams a `[client]` stanza into a `mktemp` 0600 defaults file and runs `SELECT 1` **as the customer's user**:
```
495:    const check = await execInput(
497:      `umask 077; f=$(mktemp) && cat > "$f" && ` +
498:        `mysql --defaults-extra-file="$f" --protocol=socket -N -B -e 'SELECT 1' ${shellQuote(name)} >/dev/null 2>&1; ` +
499:        `rc=$?; rm -f "$f"; exit $rc`,
500:      `[client]\nuser=${user}\npassword=${password}\n`,
503:    if (check.code !== 0) throw new Error(`the generated database credentials did not work when tested — ...`);
```
Postgres branch (507–512) deliberately has **no** probe, with the gap documented in-line ("nothing in the catalogue provisions PostgreSQL"). Note also `provisionDb` uses `CREATE DATABASE` **without** `IF NOT EXISTS` (comment at 483–484), whereas `dbCreate:106–108` uses `IF NOT EXISTS` + `ALTER USER` — so `dbCreate` will happily re-point an existing user.

**Helper locations** (all in **`/opt/nxeon/lib/ssh-exec.ts`**, all `export`ed, and already imported by `worker/databases.ts` lines 5–16):
| helper | file | line | exported | signature |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `exec` | lib/ssh-exec.ts | 114 | yes | `(conn: Client, command: string, timeoutMs: number) => Promise<SshResult>` |
| `execInput` | lib/ssh-exec.ts | 149 | yes | `(conn: Client, command: string, input: string, timeoutMs: number) => Promise<SshResult>` (does `stream.end(input)` at 180) |
| `shellQuote` | lib/ssh-exec.ts | 101 | yes | `(s: string) => string` |
| `assertIdent` | lib/ssh-exec.ts | 64 | yes | `(v: string, what: string) => void`, guards `IDENT_RE = /^[A-Za-z0-9_]{1,32}$/` (line 45) |
| `why` | **worker/apps.ts** | **360** | **NO — module-private** | `(r: { stdout: string; stderr: string }) => string` |
| `assertInertSecret` | worker/apps.ts | 355 | **NO — module-private** | `(secret: string, what: string) => void`, `/^[A-Za-z0-9]{8,128}$/` |

So reusing the probe in `worker/databases.ts` needs `why` and `assertInertSecret` exported (or duplicated); everything else is already imported there. `SshResult` type is exported at line 107.

---

## 9. Email-domain verification uses the system resolver — **CLAIM TRUE**

**(a) TRUE.**

**(b) `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-email-hosting.ts`**:
```
5:import { resolveTxt, resolveMx } from "node:dns/promises";
464:    const txt = await resolveTxt(`_nxeon-verify.${domain}`);
474:    const mx = await resolveMx(domain);
```
Bare top-level functions → `/etc/resolv.conf` + `/etc/nsswitch.conf` + `/etc/hosts`, exactly the trap documented in `lib/mail/deliverability.ts:12–28`.

**(c)** Containing export: `export async function verifyEmailDomain(subscriptionId: string): Promise<Result>` at **line 440**. This is genuinely the mailbox gate — the flag it writes (`verified: true`, line 490) is what's checked at **line 599** (`addMailbox`) and **line 666** (mailbox retry path), both returning `"Verify this domain first…"`.

**(d) Verification the claim missed** (real, but orthogonal to the resolver): the action is ownership-checked (445), rate-limited 6/60s (450–453), requires the exact token `nxeon-verify=<token>` (459, 466) and correctly joins multi-chunk TXT records (466), and MX is explicitly **corroboration only** — `if (!tokenFound)` at 480 rejects even when `mxOk` is true (comment at 471). Also, this same file **already imports the correct helper** at line 26 and uses it at 559 for the deliverability self-check — so the authoritative path is one import away, it is just not on the security-relevant gate.

**Authoritative helpers in `/opt/nxeon/lib/mail/deliverability.ts`:**
- **`export async function checkDeliverability(opts: { domain: string; mailHost: string; spfInclude: string; spfExpected: string; dmarcExpected: string; dkim: { selector: string; txt: string } | null }): Promise<DeliverabilityReport>`** — **line 159**. The only exported resolver-using function.
- `async function authoritativeResolver(domain: string): Promise<{ resolver: Resolver; nameservers: string[] } | { error: string }>` — **line 88**, **NOT exported**. This is the actual reusable primitive: walks parent zones via pinned `BOOTSTRAP_RESOLVERS = ["1.1.1.1", "8.8.8.8", "9.9.9.9"]` (line 33), resolves NS→A/AAAA (111–115), returns a `Resolver` pinned to the zone's own nameservers (121–122).
- Also private: `bootstrapResolver()` (65), `txtAt(resolver, host)` (131), `parentZones` (74), `joinTxt` (127).

To fix item 9 properly, `authoritativeResolver` (and optionally `txtAt`) must be exported; `checkDeliverability` alone doesn't expose an arbitrary-TXT lookup for `_nxeon-verify.<domain>`.

---

## 10. Provision reports RUNNING with no readiness probe — **CLAIM TRUE**

**(a) TRUE**, all three sub-claims.

**(b) `/opt/nxeon/worker/index.ts`**, containing function **`async function provision(job: Job)` at line 193** (module-private; registered as `PROVISION: provision` at **line 772**).

Swallowed snippet write, **276–278** verbatim:
```
276:  await writeFile(`${SNIPPET_DIR}/nxeon-${vmid}.yaml`, snippet, "utf8").catch((e) =>
277:    console.error("[worker] snippet write failed", e)
278:  );
```
`.catch` returns `undefined`, execution continues, and line 292 then sets `cicustom: \`vendor=${SNIPPET_STORAGE}:snippets/nxeon-${vmid}.yaml\`` pointing at a file that may not exist. A missing vendor snippet loses root-SSH config, the guest agent, START-WITH-CLAUDE.md, the MOTD and the whole setup script — silently, to console only.

Last real action before success, **315–316**:
```
315:  const startUpid = await conn.post(`/nodes/${conn.node}/qemu/${vmid}/status/start`, {});
316:  await conn.waitForTask(startUpid);
```
`waitForTask` only confirms the **Proxmox task** finished (i.e. qemu accepted `start`) — not that the guest booted, not that cloud-init ran, not that sshd is listening. Immediately after:
```
318:  await db.server.update({ where: { id: server.id }, data: { status: "RUNNING" } });
```
and the copy-pasteable credential line, **320–328**:
```
320:  const sshLine = dedicated
321:    ? `ssh root@${dedicated.address}`
322:    : `ssh root@${server.node?.publicIp ?? process.env.PUBLIC_IP} -p ${sshPort}`;
323:  await notify(
325:    `Server ${server.hostname} is ready`,
```
No `agent/ping`, no port-22 probe, no cloud-init status check anywhere between 316 and 328.

**(c)** `provision` → `notify` (`/opt/nxeon/worker/index.ts:547`).

**(d) Missed verification:** clone and resize *are* awaited via `waitForTask` (271, 308), the VM-exists idempotency check at 256–261 is real, and IP/port allocation is transactionally claimed (239–242). Also `provisionMailbox`-style guest-agent access **already exists in the codebase** — `/opt/nxeon/lib/proxmox.ts:356` calls `/nodes/${node}/qemu/${vmid}/agent/get-fsinfo` and is explicitly documented (lines 330–336) as returning `null` "when the agent isn't ready". That is a ready-made liveness signal the provision path does not use. Note the SANDBOX branch (197–213) writes `status: "RUNNING"` at line 205 by design and is out of scope.

---

## 11. Claude Code install is best-effort `|| true` — **CLAIM TRUE**

**(a) TRUE.**

**(b) `/opt/nxeon/worker/index.ts`**, verbatim **113–114**:
```
113:      "npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code || true",
114:      "command -v claude >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo 'Claude Code installed' >> /var/log/nxeon-setup.log || true",
```
Line 114 *does* probe — but the result goes only to a log file on the guest, and the trailing `|| true` neutralises even that. Nothing reads `/var/log/nxeon-setup.log`: grepping the whole repo (excluding node_modules/docs) for `nxeon-setup.log` returns only `worker/index.ts:114` and `worker/index.ts:186`. There is no `claudeCodeInstalled` column — `prisma/schema.prisma` has no Claude-install field (only `ClaudeBuild`, the unrelated AI-builder model at line 639).

**(c) Containing function:** `function buildCloudInit(server: any): string` — **line 92**, module-private. Guard at line 105: `if (addons.claudeCode !== false)` (opt-out, so it is on by default). The Node bootstrap above it (109–112) is itself a chain of `||` fallbacks ending in `|| true`.

**Delivery path (cloud-init vendor snippet, background):**
1. `buildCloudInit` joins the commands into `const script = ["#!/bin/bash", "set -x", ...setup].join("\n")` (line 123).
2. The returned `#cloud-config` (159–187) embeds it as a `write_files` entry: `- path: /root/nxeon-setup.sh` / `permissions: "0755"` (179–182).
3. It is executed **detached** — `runcmd` line **186**: `- nohup /root/nxeon-setup.sh > /var/log/nxeon-setup.log 2>&1 &`. So even cloud-init's own exit status can't reflect it.
4. `provision` writes it to `${SNIPPET_DIR}/nxeon-${vmid}.yaml` (line 276 — the same swallowed `.catch` from item 10) and attaches it via `cicustom: vendor=${SNIPPET_STORAGE}:snippets/nxeon-${vmid}.yaml` (line 292). `SNIPPET_DIR` = `/tank/backup/snippets`, `SNIPPET_STORAGE` = `backup` (190–191).

**Items 10 and 11 compound:** if the write at 276 fails, the snippet never exists, Claude Code is never installed, *and* the customer still gets "Server … is ready" plus a MOTD promising it — because nothing between 276 and 328 checks anything.

**(d) The product-side assertions** (the doc says 7; current source has 9 hits across 4 files, plus 2 marketing-page variants):

| file | line | text |
|---|---|---|
| `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/claude-code/ClaudeCodeHub.tsx` | 277 | `"Claude Code is pre-installed on every Nxeon server. …"` |
| same | 287 | `Already installed` (green emerald badge, 286–288) |
| same | 341 | `{ kind: "ok", text: "Welcome to your Nxeon server — Claude Code is pre-installed." }` |
| same | 353 | `"…Deploy one and Claude Code will be waiting on it."` |
| `/opt/nxeon/lib/ai-build.ts` | 70 | `"Type claude and press Enter. Claude Code is already installed on your VPS. …"` |
| same | 97 | `{ kind: "ok", text: "Welcome to Nxeon VPS - Claude Code is pre-installed" }` |
| same | 160 | same string |
| `/opt/nxeon/worker/index.ts` | 129 | `"## Build anything with Claude Code — it's already installed"` (→ `/root/START-WITH-CLAUDE.md`) |
| same | 153 | `Nxeon — Claude Code is pre-installed on this server.` (→ `/etc/profile.d/nxeon-welcome.sh` MOTD, printed on every interactive login) |
| `/opt/nxeon/app/(marketing)/vibe-coding/page.tsx` | 210 | `"…Claude Code, built into every Nxeon VPS…"` |
| same | 371 | `"Every Nxeon VPS comes with Claude Code ready to go. …"` |

Lines 129 and 153 are the sharpest: they are written **by the same function that made the install best-effort**, into the guest, so a server where `npm install -g` failed greets the customer on login with a claim the same file knows may be false. One partial mitigation exists — `ClaudeCodeHub.tsx:369` offers manual install instructions, but it is framed as "Created your server before this feature?", i.e. it presents the gap as historical rather than as a possible install failure.

The stale-doc reference itself is `/opt/nxeon/docs/QA-JOURNEY.md:285`, which cites `worker/index.ts:113-114` — still exactly correct.
